clues: This is the capital of a small island land in Europe. It sits between two deep harbours, and it is the farthest south capital in all of Europe.
This city was named the sunniest city in Europe in 2016. Its bright days set it apart from grey capitals far to the north.
Its stone buildings went up in the 1500s, built by knights. Those knights had held the island through a great siege by Ottoman foes.
It packs 320 old monuments into a space smaller than many parks. People call it an open-air museum for that rich, packed past.
At just 0.61 square kilometres in size, this is the smallest capital city in the EU.
